title: Putative microfossils of the Nuvvuagittuq belt (reported 2017)
summary: In 2017 a team led from University College London reported tiny hematite-filled tubes and filaments in jasper from the Nuvvuagittuq belt in northern Quebec, interpreting them as microbes from a seafloor hydrothermal vent. They gave a minimum age of 3.77 billion years, possibly up to 4.28; both the biological origin and the age are disputed.

uncertainty.note: The authors give 3.77 billion years as the youngest (minimum) age, based on dating of intrusions; their oldest estimate is 4.28 billion years from a more contested samarium-neodymium method. Skeptics doubt the minimum age as well. The range runs from 3.77 to 4.28 billion years ago.
